result.title: When Does Optical Context Compression Pay Off? A Decode-Aware Cost Analysis of Reasoning VLMs
result.summary: Rendering long text as images lets a vision-language model (VLM) read a document with fewer input tokens, and evaluations often count mainly these prefill tokens. We show that for reasoning models this accounting is incomplete. Across five models and two long-context benchmarks, reading the rendered document makes the model think longer: decode length grows by 1.5-3.5x on the four general-purpose VLMs tested, and under typical output pricing this decode tax makes image input more expensive than text for two of the five models on QuALITY. Unrecoverable information loss is not sufficient to explain the tax at moderate compression: Qwen's OCR of the same images recovers 98.7% of words, and feeding Kimi-K3 its own transcription as text restores text-mode reasoning length and accuracy. Whether compression pays off reduces to an exchange rate, (1-1/c)/(r-1), that must exceed the workload's price-weighted ratio of output to input tokens; this accounting decomposition shows why Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash can benefit and Qwen and GLM cannot. None of the training-free signals we test predicts the tax before generation. As a practical heuristic, an image-first policy that sends only inputs with a per-input compression ratio of at least 1.6 to images and falls back to text once image-mode reasoning costs as much as the input's prefill saving cuts the bill by 6-14% on Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at an accuracy cost of 0.3-1.2 points; on QuALITY, asking for a reasoning budget on both paths is a stronger lever.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在五个模型、两个长上下文基准上分析把长文本渲染成图像的「光学上下文压缩」，发现推理 VLM 的图像输入会带来 1.5–3.5 倍解码长度增长，并给出压缩比与输入输出价格之比构成的收益换算条件及图像优先回退策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及视觉输入路径的收益与成本核算：OCR 可恢复 98.7% 词仍出现推理变长，说明视觉旁路的问题不止信息坍缩，可作为 THINK/LOOK/STOP 成本权衡与视觉证据筛选的对照；其模型与基准能否外推到 latent 推理状态尚待核查。
